content: The references provided are a comprehensive list of studies, clinical trials, and reviews related to HIV treatment, drug resistance, and the use of antiretroviral therapies, particularly focusing on dolutegravir and other integrase inhibitors. 1. Wainberg MA and Han YS (2015) explored the potential for drug resistance to dolutegravir in initial HIV therapy. Their findings were published in Frontiers in Pharmacology and provide insights into the robustness of dolutegravir against resistance development. 2. Blanco J, Oldenbuettel C, Thomas R, Mallolas J, Wolf E, Brenner B, et al. investigated the mechanisms of resistance in patients who failed dolutegravir monotherapy. Their findings were presented in a webcast accessed on July 1, 2017. 3. Wijting I, Rokx C, Boucher C, de Vries-Sluijs D, Schurink K, Andrinopoulou E, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial to evaluate dolutegravir as a maintenance monotherapy for HIV-1. The results were shared in an abstract and poster session accessed on July 1, 2017. 4. The UK Collaborative Group on HIV Drug Resistance (2010) analyzed the long-term probability of detecting drug-resistant HIV in treatment-naïve patients initiating combination antiretroviral therapy. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 5. Maggiolo F, Gulminetti R, Pagnucco L, Digaetano M, Benatti S, Valenti D, et al. (2017) studied the efficacy of lamivudine/dolutegravir dual therapy in virologically suppressed HIV-infected patients. Their research was published in BMC Infectious Diseases. 6. Gubavu C, Prazuck T, Niang M, Buret J, Mille C, Guinard J, et al. (2016) demonstrated that dolutegravir-based monotherapy or dual therapy maintains high levels of viral suppression even in highly experienced HIV-1-infected patients. This study was published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 7. Borghetti A, Baldin G, Ciccullo A, Gagliardini R, Davino A, Mondi A, et al. (2016) reported on virological control and metabolic improvements in HIV-infected patients switching to lamivudine/dolutegravir dual therapy. Their findings appeared in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 8. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd edition) provides a framework for developing evidence-based guidelines, accessed on July 1, 2017. 9. The WHO HIV Drug Resistance Report (2017) outlines the prevalence and impact of pretreatment HIV drug resistance globally, accessed on July 1, 2017. 10. Kaplan S, Oosthuizen C, Stinson K, Little F, Euvrard J, Osler M, et al. examined disengagement from antiretroviral therapy in Khayelitsha, South Africa. Their findings were presented in a session accessed on July 1, 2017. 11. Phillips AN, Stover J, Cambiano V, Nakagawa F, Jordan MR, Pillay D, et al. (2017) assessed the impact of HIV drug resistance on mortality, new infections, and antiretroviral therapy program costs in sub-Saharan Africa. Their study was published in Journal of Infectious Diseases. 12. Hofstra LM, Sánchez Rivas E, Nijhuis M, Bank LEA, Wilkinson E, Kelly K, et al. (2017) reported high rates of transmitted drug-resistant HIV in Aruba, which reduced susceptibility to WHO-recommended first-line regimens. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 13. Hamers RL, Schuurman R, Sigaloff KC, Wallis CL, Kityo C, Siwale M, et al. (2012) evaluated the effect of pretreatment HIV-1 drug resistance on treatment outcomes in sub-Saharan Africa. Their multicenter cohort study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 14. Luebbert J, Tweya H, Phiri S, Chawedza T, Mwafilaso J, Hosseinipour MC, et al. (2012) investigated virological failure and drug resistance in patients on antiretroviral therapy after treatment interruption in Malawi. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 15. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses informing the WHO guidelines on public health responses to pretreatment HIV drug resistance were accessed on July 1, 2017. 16. Lockman S, Hughes MD, McIntyre J, Zheng Y, Chipato T, Conradie F, et al. (2010) studied antiretroviral therapies in women exposed to single-dose nevirapine. Their findings were published in The New England Journal of Medicine. 17. Kantor R, Smeaton L, Vardhanabhuti S, Hudelson SE, Wallis CL, Tripathy S, et al. (2015) found that pretreatment HIV drug resistance and subtype C were independently associated with virologic failure. Their results were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 18. Lai CC, Hung CC, Chen MY, Sun HY, Lu CL, Tseng YT, et al. (2012) analyzed trends in transmitted drug resistance and its impact on treatment response in Taiwan. Their study was published in Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy. 19. Kuritzkes DR, Lalama CM, Ribaudo HJ, Marcial M, Meyer WA III, Shikuma C, et al. (2008) demonstrated that preexisting resistance to non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors predicts virologic failure in treatment-naïve HIV-1-infected subjects. Their findings were published in Journal of Infectious Diseases. 20. Ávila-Ríos S, García-Morales C, Matías-Florentino M, Romero-Mora KA, Tapia-Trejo D, Quiroz-Morales VSS, et al. (2016) assessed pretreatment HIV drug resistance in Mexico and its impact on first-line therapy effectiveness. Their study was published in The Lancet HIV. 21. Bansi L, Geretti AM, Dunn D, Hill T, Green H, Fearnhill E, et al. (2010) evaluated the impact of transmitted drug resistance on treatment outcomes of first-line highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART). Their findings were published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 22. Boender TS, Hoenderboom BM, Sigaloff KC, Hamers RL, Wellington M, Shamu T, et al. (2015) reported that pretreatment HIV drug resistance increases regimen switching in sub-Saharan Africa. Their study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases. 23. Chaix ML, Desquilbet L, Descamps D, Costagliola D, Deveau C, Galimand J, et al. (2007) analyzed responses to HAART in French patients with resistant HIV-1 treated at primary infection. Their findings were published in Antiviral Therapy. 24. Crowell CS, Maiga AI, Sylla M, Taiwo B, Kone N, Oron AP, et al. reported high rates of baseline drug resistance and virologic failure among ART-naïve HIV-infected children in Mali. Their study was published in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. 25. Ngo-Giang-Huong N, Wittkop L, Judd A, Reiss P, Goetghebuer T, Duiculescu D, et al. (2016) examined the prevalence and effect of pretreatment drug resistance on virological response in HIV-infected children. Their findings were published in BMC Infectious Diseases. 26. Shet A, Neogi U, Kumarasamy N, De Costa A, Shastri S, Rewari BB, et al. (2015) evaluated virological efficacy with first-line antiretroviral therapy in India, identifying predictors of viral failure and evidence of viral resuppression. Their study was published in Tropical Medicine & International Health. 27. Hong SY, Jonas A, De Klerk M, Shiningavamwe A, Desta T, Badi A, et al. (2015) conducted population-based surveillance of HIV drug resistance emerging on treatment in Namibia. Their findings were published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 28. Phanuphak P, Sirivichayakul S, Jiamsakul A, Sungkanuparph S, Kumarasamy N, Lee MP, et al. (2014) studied transmitted drug resistance and treatment outcomes in non-subtype B HIV-1-infected patients in Southeast Asia. Their findings were published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 29. Wittkop L, Günthard HF, de Wolf F, Dunn D, Cozzi-Lepri A, de Luca A, et al. (2011) analyzed the effect of transmitted drug resistance on virological and immunological responses to initial combination antiretroviral therapy in Europe. Their study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 30. Boender TS, Sigaloff KC, Rinke de Wit TF, van Hensbroek MB, Ndembi N, et al. (2016) reported high levels of pretreatment HIV drug resistance and treatment failure in Nigerian children. Their findings were published in Journal of the International AIDS Society. This list continues with similar detailed interpretations of the remaining references.
